newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's parliament elects new president.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's parliament elects new president.

text.p: Janez Podbonik of Slovenia's conservative People's Party was elected as the new president of parliament on Tuesday in the first session of the legislature after the country's second general election three weeks ago.
Podobnik, who was the only candidate, received 82 out of 86 votes cast.

Slovenia's second general election after its independence from Yugoslavia in 1991 yielded a tight result, giving a loose alliance of three rightist parties, the so-called "Spring" coalition, 45 of the parliament's 90 seats.

The centre-left Liberal Democrats of current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek emerged as the strongest single party with 25 seats, but will have to find a coalition partner if they want to stay in power.
The People's Party, the most influential member of the "Spring" coalition, came second with 19 seats. It is led by Marjan Podobnik, brother of the newly elected head of parliament.
Slovenian President Milan Kucan is expected to propose a candidate for the post of the next prime minister within a month, after which parliament will have to vote on his suggestion.
